text:
sara: FYI Sam (customer) is seeing very slow responses on dedicated-hosted tenant acme-eu after a traffic spike. 95th p90 jump and a bunch of 502/429s.
sam-customer: API errors started ~09:07 UTC, errors look like 502 gateway and occasional 429s. App logs show request queued for 6s before failing.
david: Can you paste a raw curl from the client? also which model/route? sara: they're hitting /v1/generate -> redwood-hosted model rwd-llama-7b, route 'prod-eu-r1'. curl below.
sam-customer: ```bash
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-XXXX" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hello","max_tokens":64}'
HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
x-request-id: rwd-req-73a
content-length: 0
```
sara: On our side the provisioning logs show attach attempts failing then a fallback to cpu fallback pods. Key lines:
```
2026-02-14T09:06:47Z attach-controller: tenant=acme-eu attach_attempt=1 status=403 "image pull denied"
2026-02-14T09:06:49Z autoscaler: tenant=acme-eu desired=12 ready=4 provisioning=0 min_replicas=2 max_replicas=20
2026-02-14T09:06:53Z runtime: fallback_to_cpu=true reason="no gpu nodes available"
2026-02-14T09:07:01Z refund-billing: tentative_hold=true tenant=acme-eu billing_state=RETRY
```
kevin: 403 on attach + billing hold looks suspicious. If billing hook flipped to RETRY it blocks certain image pulls until accounting is reconciled. That plus our cold chain means autoscaler won't request more GPUs immediately.
julia: Is that a known interaction? ops-bot: note: alert autoscaler_attach_failures high for tenant acme-eu (alert_id: A-9821)
sara: Repro steps we used:
1) set min_replicas=2, max_replicas=20 for tenant
2) send a synthetic spike (20 req/s, 4k token context) for 90s
3) observe attach-controller logs above
4) observe fallback pods created after 10-15s and higher 429s from route
kevin: Quick mitigation: temporarily bump min_replicas to 6 to have warm seats and flip billing hold resolution. But need root cause: why did billing hook trigger during normal usage? david: Could be an auth rotation that failed right when a new node tried to attach; attach-controller gets 403 from registry because service-account token got rotated and billing stack applied a conservative policy.
sam-customer: we did a payment retry earlier today, but it completed successfully. why would there be a RETRY hold? sara: looks like a race: billing state transitions to RETRY during a reconciliation window when a new attach happened -> blocks imagepull until the next reconcile ( ~30s ). Combined with autoscaler backoff this yields 20-30s scaleup lag and lots of 429/502 on the client side.
julia: This is different from typical "warm-pool" problems — it's an attach-auth/billing gating issue. We should document and patch.
kevin: Short-term runbook:
- set min_replicas higher for affected tenant
- nudge billing to fast-reconcile (manual override)
- whitelist registry pull for attach-controller for a short window
Long-term:
- remove billing-state dependency for critical attach flow OR make attach retries ignore transient billing(RETRY) for up to 60s
- add metric: attach_blocked_by_billing_count
- reduce autoscaler backoff when attach failures are non-capacity (eg 403)
david: I've re-run the synthetic spike after bumping min_replicas -> no 502s, p95 is stable. I'll open an infra PR to treat billing RETRY as transient in attach logic.
sara: i've alerted support engineering and customer success, told Sam we're doing mitigation and will follow up. Sam: thanks, appreciate the fast triage :thumbsup:
ops-bot: incident-note created: INC-2026-0214-attach-billing-block, severity=low, owner=david
kevin: tagging @eng-infra for a follow-up change to the attach controller.
julia: filing a CSEKB (customer-facing explanation) draft after infra PR merges.
